issues.translation_quote: Timofeev has blown the fuses again!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but later 'Сегодня Вы пережгли пробки, а завтра пережжете весь дом' is rendered 'blow up the whole building', which changes burning out fuses into explosion and loses the escalation logic of the joke.

issues.source_quote: Товарищ Тимофеев, когда это кончится? ... Я спрашиваю, когда кончатся ваши безответственные опыты
issues.translation_quote: when will this end? - I'm just finishing.
issues.justification: The comic double meaning of 'кончится/заканчиваю' is kept only partially; the follow-up clarification works but the pun is flat.
Context is the dentist being called while treating a patient; the line is unclear and the humor of the dentist's patient is lost without any cue.

issues.source_quote: Я - артист больших и малых академических театров!
issues.translation_quote: I am an actor of the Bolshoi and Maly academic theaters!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but Bunsha/Miloslavsky's evasive joke is fine; however 'Меня терзают смутные сомнения' is rendered 'tormented by vague suspicions', losing the quoted literary-parody allusion (Bulgakov/Gogol reference style) but acceptable. The more serious issue is 'Honorary title of Building of High Domestic Culture' which sounds like a Soviet calque without humor cue.

Fine; but 'Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!' is rendered 'Order not my execution' which is stilted and mistranslates the idiom ('do not order me executed' is a formulaic plea) and sounds awkward.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Order not my execution, Great Sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: Overly archaic pseudo-Elizabethan 'thou/hath' register is applied inconsistently and to the wrong characters, producing an unnatural, uneven voice; the Russian is Muscovite courtly speech, not Shakespearean.

issues.source_quote: Не демон я! ... Ой, не лги! Царю лжешь!
issues.translation_quote: Say once more, thou art no demon? ... Oh, lie not! Thou liest to the Tsar!
issues.justification: Thou/thee forms are inconsistently applied; in the same scene Ivan sometimes speaks modern English ('Be thou hale' next to 'Cheers!'), breaking the character voice.

issues.translation_quote: We want a goal! A goal!..
issues.justification: 'Шайбу, шайбу' is a hockey chant; 'goal' loses the puck/hockey reference and the incongruity is not carried, and 'Tsar!' chant is not explained.
Minor tone shift; but more seriously 'Бунша' appears in the subtitle as 'Bunsha' while the speaker earlier is Timofeev and the character name is inconsistent with 'Boris' forms.

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг ... Интурист хорошо говорит!
issues.justification: 'Интурист' is the Soviet agency for foreign tourists; the joke that Bunsha treats the ambassador as a tourist is acceptable, but the German gibberish is actually mis-rendered/garbled and 'So vat to tell my king?' invents an accent not present in the Russian.

issues.source_quote: Они любят друг друга. Ну и пусть будут счастливы.
issues.justification: Fine; however 'Лови́т?' → 'Are they being hunted?' and 'Как поймают, Якина на кол посадить!' → 'impale Yakin' are acceptable, but 'Ух, добрый ты человек!' → 'Oh, thou art a kind man!' loses the colloquial warmth.

Source pun is that the interrogator asks if he 'took' Shpak's apartment (брал квартиру) and Ivan lists cities he took; translation switches to 'took Shpak' rather than 'Shpak's apartment', breaking the pun.
Acceptable; but 'Профессион де фуа' → 'Profession de foi!' misses the intended pun/mock-correction of 'профессиональная обязанность' with French and is left without comic effect.

issues.source_quote: Давай с тобой на брудершафт выпьем!
issues.justification: 'Drink to brotherhood' is unnatural; 'drink to our friendship' or 'seal it with a drink' is more idiomatic.
Grammatically broken in English ('One kidneys'); even as comedy it reads as an error.

issues.source_quote: Сделал мне предложение и мы сейчас улетаем
issues.justification: 'Трогай!' is rendered as 'Drive on!', which is plausible but the scene does not involve driving; better 'Off we go!'.
Fine, but the name is inconsistently handled (Georges / George) across lines; keep one form.

issues.source_quote: Они так утомляют, эти скандалы. Три раза я разводилась.
issues.justification: Fine, but 'выписывай' as 'take me off the residence registry' is an overly technical rendering lacking Soviet-specific clarity for audiences.
